title: Canonical route remap during canary rollout recording usage against legacy alias
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Summary:
During canary rollouts that remap route aliases to new backend variants, a subset of requests are being attributed to the legacy route alias in billing and quota accounting. This causes (1) quotas to be decremented on the wrong route/credential, (2) inconsistent per-route usage dashboards, and (3) customers to see spurious quota exhaustion or unexpected billing lines in their invoices.

Observed behavior:
- Canary policy maps canonical route "model.chat.v2" to legacy alias "model.chat.v1-legacy" for 10% of traffic for a short window.
- Real requests served by the new variant show up in the per-route usage metrics and billing pipeline as originating from the legacy alias.
- Enforcement: per-route throttles incorrectly trigger for orgs that are near their quota on the legacy alias while the actual canonical route still has headroom.

Impact:
- Multiple customers reported transient 429s during canaries and saw usage lines in billing for routes they thought were inactive.
- Internal dashboards report a surplus of usage on legacy aliases during rollouts, leading to noise in anomaly detection and evasion of regression alerts.
- High potential for incorrect overage billing if not remediated before major product launches.

Reproduction steps (minimal):
1) Create two route aliases A (legacy) and B (canonical).
2) Configure canary rollout: route B -> backend-new for 10% traffic while B -> backend-old for rest.
3) Trigger a steady stream of short requests (token light) through B.
4) Observe emitted usage events in metrics pipeline and billing consumer; some events are labelled with alias A.

Logs / evidence:
- Edge trace: routing decision shows canonical->new-variant, but the subsequent metrics envelope includes route_alias: "model.chat.v1-legacy".
- Timeline correlations show that emitter timestamps fall in the 50-200ms window after routing decision and before mapping refresh acknowledgement.
- Metric shard snapshots (dashboard link): https://dash.internal/redwood/usage/ENG-973210
- Example trace id: trace-20251103-7c9b2f

Preliminary root-cause hypothesis:
The metrics emission path samples route metadata from a per-request context that is mutated by an async remapping reconciliation routine. During canaries we perform a remap (atomic update to the route mapping table) then launch a background remap-ack collector which updates a local emitter cache. There is a race where the emitter reads a fallback alias value from the local cache if the remap-ack has not propagated to the emitter worker, causing stale alias labels to be attached to emitted usage events. The rate engine consumes those labels and attributes usage to the wrong key/route.

Proposed fix options considered:
- A: Make route labels immutable once set at routing decision time; stash the canonical label into the request context and force metric emitter to use that snapshot. (preferred: minimal surface)
- B: Add synchronous flush of remap-ack to emitter workers during rollout switches. (high coordination cost, latency risk)
- C: Post-process aggregated usage events in billing pipeline to remap aliases using eventual consistency heuristics. (workaround; doesn't fix enforcement path and might double-charge)

Decision so far:
- Implement option A: record canonical route id at the time of routing decision and ensure the emitter reads from that snapshot. This avoids extra cross-worker sync and prevents labeling races.

Work items / acceptance criteria:
- Add unit tests for emitter to assert label immutability under concurrent remap updates.
- End-to-end test demonstrating no legacy alias labels when canary toggles at 1%, 10%, 50% traffic.
- Monitor rollout for 48h after merge: per-alias usage deviation <= 0.5% compared to expected traffic split.
- Create migration job to reclassify suspect events emitted in the last 7 days (coord with billing team).

Rollout plan:
1) Small patch in runtime: stash route_id in request_context (canary internally).
2) Deploy to staging and run synthetic canaries; run billing pipeline consumer in shadow mode.
3) Gradual rollout to 10% of hosts; monitor per-route usage and throttles.
4) Full rollout if no regressions for 48h.

Notes / follow-ups:
- Billing team needs a temporary credits policy for affected customers from last 7 days. (PM: @Evan Carter)
- Add observability: emit "route_label_source" tag (routing_snapshot|cache_read) to help debug future cases.
- Consider a broader audit of other mutable meta used by emitters (client_id, org_alias) to avoid similar races.
